simple.meaning: רָצוֹן (râtsôwn) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “delight (especially as shown).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 56 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, 2 Chronicles, and 9 more, beginning at Genesis 49:6. Its contexts include offering, sacrifice, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָצוֹן (H7522).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָצוֹן (râtsôwn) / H7522 is traced through Genesis 49:6, Exodus 28:38, Leviticus 1:3, Leviticus 19:5 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H7522. ratson רָצוֺן noun [masculine] goodwill, favour, acceptance, will ; — absolute ׳ר Deut 33:23 +; construct רְצוֺן Psa 145:19 +; suffix רְצוֺנִי Isa 60:10 , רְצֹנוֺ Dan 8:4 +, etc.; — 1 goodwill, favour: a. of God , Deut 33:16 ; Isa 60:10 ; Psalm 5:13; Psa 30:6 ; 30:8 ; Psalm 51:20; 89:18 ; 106:4 ; Prov 8:35 ; 12:2 ; 18:22 ; ר ׳עֵת Isa 49:8 ; Psa 69:14 ; ר ׳יוֺם Isa 58:5 ; ׳שְׁנַתרֿ 61:2 ; || בְּרָכָה Deut 33:23 ; opposed to תּוֺעֵבָה Prov 11:1 , 20 ; 12:22 ; 15:8 . b. of men: in General Prov 10:32 ; 11:27 ; 14:9 ; of kings 14:35 ; 16:13 , 15 ; 19:12 . 2 acceptance , of persons, offering sacrifice, יהוה לפני לרצון Exod 28:38 (P); with ל person for acceptance for him before ׳י ; with suffix person לרצנוֺ Lev 1:3 ; abbreviated לָכֶם לְרָצוֺן 22:20 , לרצנכם 19:5 ; 22:19 , 29 ; 23:11 , לצֵּון 22:21 ; Isa 56:7 ; Jer 6:20 ; Psalm 19:15 (of words; compare Hosea 14:3 ); רצון על Isa 60:7 (read לְ , so Manuscripts, see Gi, also Du), רצון Mal 2:13 . 3 will, desire, pleasure: a. of God , ר ׳עשׂה do his will Ezra 10:11 ; Psa 40:9 ; 103:21 ; 143:10 . b. of man , כרצונוֺ עשׂה do according to his will , exactly as he pleased, Dan 8:4 ; 11:3 , 16 , 36 ; Neh 9:24 ; Est 1:8 ; 9:5 , compare Neh 9:37 ; desire Psa 145:16 ; 145:19 ; 2Chr 15:15 ; = self-will Gen 49:6 (poem).

I saw the ram pushing westward, northward, and southward. No animals could stand before him. There wasn’t any who could deliver out of his hand; but he did according to his will, and magnified himself.
A mighty king will stand up, who will rule with great dominion, and do according to his will.
But he who comes against him will do according to his own will, and no one will stand before him. He will stand in the glorious land, and destruction will be in his hand.
